fun_facts: Jonathan Taylor was born in Salem, New Jersey.
Jonathan Taylor said he hadn’t played organized sports before football; in high school, he played football and ran track.
As a freshman at Wisconsin, Jonathan Taylor broke the FBS freshman rushing record with 1,977 yards.
Jonathan Taylor was the fastest player to reach 5,000 rushing yards in FBS history, doing so before the end of his junior season.
Jonathan Taylor finished his college career with 6,174 rushing yards, the most in FBS history through a player’s junior season.
Jonathan Taylor won the Doak Walker Award twice and was a unanimous first-team All-American twice.

excerpts: A year ago, Wisconsin didn't know what it had in Taylor, who in 2017 reached rarefied air at the program's loftiest position: running back. He broke Adrian Peterson's FBS freshman rushing record with 1,977 yards, eclipsed 100 yards in 10 of 14 games with three 200-yard efforts, and finished sixth in the Heisman Trophy voting. An easy choice for Big Ten Freshman of the Year, Taylor earned second-team AP All-America honors and consideration for both the Doak Walker and Maxwell awards.
